section_summary: This section concerns Japan’s petroleum supply and proposed government control of its oil industry in 1932–33. Embassy reports and oil company correspondence examine dependence on imported oil, competition from Soviet supplies, gasoline price controls, and the possible effects of a monopoly or licensing system on foreign firms. The section also records efforts to raise these concerns at the London Economic Conference.

subfiles.title: Charge slip for decimal file 894.6363
subfiles.about: Records the file’s charge information.
subfiles.summary: Charge slip for file 894.6363, dated March 25, 1946.

subfiles.title: File note on rumored Soviet-Japanese petroleum agreement
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram concerning a rumored agreement for Soviet oil supplies to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a September 1932 telegram about a rumored Soviet-Japanese petroleum agreement.

subfiles.title: Japan’s Oil Problems
subfiles.about: Surveys Japan’s oil supply, domestic controls, Soviet contracts, and the position of American and British oil firms.
subfiles.summary: Grew describes Japan’s limited domestic oil production, reliance on American and Dutch imports, and naval supplies from Fushun and North Sakhalin. He examines gasoline tariffs and price controls that disadvantage Socony-Vacuum and Rising Sun, tentative Soviet supply contracts, and the prospect of foreign firms building Japanese refineries. He also discusses wartime reserves and possible controls in Manchuria. Page 19 is the despatch’s summary.

subfiles.title: Correction to Japan’s Oil Problems
subfiles.about: Requests correction of the earlier despatch’s statement on crude oil and gasoline duties.
subfiles.summary: Grew supplies replacement wording on tariff rates and their effect on gasoline importers.

subfiles.title: Tentative Japanese oil monopoly or licensing plans
subfiles.about: Reports tentative Japanese plans for an oil monopoly or licensing system and diplomatic concern over foreign interests.
subfiles.summary: Grew describes two Mining Bureau proposals that could eventually displace foreign oil distributors. British, Dutch, and American representatives have sought clarification; the Dutch minister also raises a possible treaty objection. Grew asks the Department to consider whether either proposal could conflict with the American treaty of commerce.

subfiles.title: File note on London discussion of foreign oil interests
subfiles.about: Cross-references Grew’s telegram about discussing foreign oil interests at the London conference.
subfiles.summary: File note points to Grew’s May 11 telegram on a proposed London discussion.

subfiles.title: Proposed London discussion of foreign oil interests
subfiles.about: Reports British suggestions to discuss foreign oil interests in Japan at the London Economic Conference.
subfiles.summary: The British Embassy and Rising Sun Petroleum have both urged a London conference discussion.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Standard Oil Company of New York
subfiles.about: Acknowledges company concerns about developments threatening its Japanese interests.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck says the Department is studying Fales’s letter and expects to reply further.

subfiles.title: Telegram to Benjamin B. Wallace
subfiles.about: Asks Wallace to meet a Socony-Vacuum representative bringing material for Feis.
subfiles.summary: Phillips asks Wallace to receive Philo Parker at the ship and pass his material to Feis.

subfiles.title: Railway delivery message concerning Wallace
subfiles.about: Reports that Wallace was apparently not aboard the specified train.
subfiles.summary: Railway and State Department representatives told Brown that Wallace was not on the train.

subfiles.title: Transmission of oil industry correspondence to Grew
subfiles.about: Forwards company letters, a conversation memorandum, cables, and a memorandum concerning Japan’s oil industry.
subfiles.summary: Phillips sends Grew copies of recent company correspondence and related Department documents.

subfiles.title: Standard Oil concerns over Japanese oil policy
subfiles.about: Warns that gasoline controls and possible monopoly or licensing measures threaten Socony-Vacuum’s Japanese investments.
subfiles.summary: Fales reports substantial losses under gasoline price controls and says proposed national oil policies jeopardize the company’s investment. He requests the Department’s views and suggests raising the matter during economic talks with Japan.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Kersey F. Coe
subfiles.about: Records discussion of a possible London meeting to protect foreign oil interests in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Coe gives Department officers cables and a memorandum on Japanese oil measures. Hornbeck favors exploring a London meeting of oil representatives and arranging delivery of the documents to Wallace; the participants also discuss treaty and legal questions.

subfiles.title: Reply to Kersey F. Coe on London consultations
subfiles.about: Advises how oil firms might consult in London and approach the American delegation.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck says the delegation has the relevant information. He recommends that oil interests meet in London first, then bring unresolved questions to their national delegations.

subfiles.title: Yokohama cable proposing oil industry meeting
subfiles.about: Proposes a London meeting among oil companies and coordinated diplomatic approaches to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The cable urges American, British, Dutch, and Japanese oil interests to seek a commercial plan protecting foreign investments and trade. It suggests government support for talks before Japan adopts a national oil policy and also notes concern about Manchuria.

subfiles.title: London cable on coordinated oil industry action
subfiles.about: Urges a joint approach by oil companies and diplomats for a statement of Japanese policy.
subfiles.summary: London representatives support a proposed oil company meeting and coordinated approaches to American, Dutch, and British officials. They fear Japanese nationalist measures could hamper foreign trade, beginning in Manchuria.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on American petroleum interests in Japan
subfiles.about: Quantifies American oil trade with Japan and sets out protections sought from Japanese policy changes.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum estimates Japan’s petroleum consumption, American exports, and Socony-Vacuum’s sales and losses. It asks for assurances on tariffs, fair treatment under price controls, refinery rights, the Open Door in Manchuria, and continued market access under any monopoly or licensing system. It advocates coordinated American, British, and Dutch action and a meeting with Japanese oil interests in London.

subfiles.title: Japan’s Oil Problems: Supplementary Information
subfiles.about: Corrects and supplements Grew’s earlier oil report on gasoline controls, Soviet oil, duties, and import shares.
subfiles.summary: Grew clarifies dates and price increases under the gasoline control agreement. He says the reported North Sakhalin Soviet contract may not yet have been signed, corrects his account of Siberian refineries, explains petroleum duty rates, and revises the American–Dutch gasoline import comparison.

subfiles.title: Japan’s Oil Problems: Current Developments
subfiles.about: Examines Japanese proposals for national control of petroleum and foreign diplomatic and company responses.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports conversations with Japanese officials and British and Dutch diplomats about the future of foreign oil firms. He describes tentative Mining Bureau plans for a government monopoly or import and refining licenses, their legislative prospects, and the national defense arguments behind them. Foreign companies fear losing their investments and consider taking the issue to the London Economic Conference. The despatch lists four enclosures, which follow.

subfiles.title: Lindley letter to Grew about oil interests
subfiles.about: Relates Lindley’s appeal to Count Uchida for assurances on British oil investment in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Lindley says Uchida confirmed that Japanese authorities were studying oil policy and would convey his concerns.

subfiles.title: Joint oil company inquiry to the Minister of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.from: Rising Sun Petroleum Company and Socony-Vacuum Corporation
subfiles.about: Asks how Japan’s industrial control law and future petroleum policy will affect foreign importers and refiners.
subfiles.summary: The companies seek guidance on whether Japan favors domestic refining, how foreign owned refineries and imported products will be treated, and whether tariffs or licenses may change. They also ask how gasoline prices, market shares, new entrants, and majority agreements will be regulated. They emphasize their existing investment and request equal standing in Japan’s oil industry.

subfiles.title: Mining Bureau cover letter answering oil company inquiry
subfiles.from: Chief of the Mine Bureau, Department of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.about: Transmits an answer to the companies’ inquiry about control of the gasoline industry.
subfiles.summary: The Mining Bureau chief encloses a response to the November 29 inquiry.
